result.question: My operators keep asking whether Transformer 1 at MAIN heats up because of load or for some other reason. Over the available window, characterize how oti, oti_a and oti_t move together with the phase currents il1, il2, il3 and inut. Tell me whether the temperature group and the current group rise and fall in the same samples. Then run an anomaly check on the temperature channels together with the currents, and list any timestamp where temperature is anomalous but current is not. Treat those timestamps as possible non-load heating, and pull the dissolved gas classification from the nearest oil sample to see whether it shows a thermal fault. Only use samples where all four current channels are non-null. If none of the temperature anomalies lines up with a thermal gas class, say that the heating looks load or ambient driven, and check ati at the same timestamps. If fewer than 4 complete samples remain after cleaning, skip the anomaly model and report only the characterization with its limits.
result.answer:
### Characterization
All **5 daily samples, January 15–19, 2024**, have non-null currents and temperature channels; none were excluded.

| Date | oti | oti_a | oti_t | il1 | il2 | il3 | inut | ati |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan 15 | 85 | 2 | 1 | 100 | 105 | 95 | 5 | 78 |
| Jan 16 | 87 | 2 | 1 | 102 | 103 | 96 | 6 | 79 |
| Jan 17 | 84 | 1 | 1 | 101 | 104 | 94 | 5 | 77 |
| Jan 18 | 86 | 2 | 1 | 100 | 106 | 95 | 5 | 78 |
| Jan 19 | 85 | 2 | 1 | 100 | 105 | 95 | 5 | 78 |

**The groups do not uniformly rise and fall together.** OTI and mean phase current move in the same direction on all four transitions, but individual currents disagree: `il2` opposes OTI on the first two transitions, while `il1` falls as OTI rises on January 18. `oti_a` changes only around January 17; `oti_t` never changes.

OTI’s same-sample correlations are **0.44 with il1, −0.23 with il2, 0.93 with il3, and 0.78 with inut**. Ambient `ati` also closely follows OTI (**r = 0.93**); OTI−ATI stays at **7–8**.

### Anomaly and gas checks
**The anomaly model could not be run:** both detector-catalog searches returned no models, and no usable dataset-file pointer was available. Therefore, temperature-only anomaly timestamps and their nearest-sample gas classifications remain **undetermined**, not “none.”

These five samples are consistent with load/ambient-related variation, but cannot establish causation or exclude thermal faults. The requested “no thermal gas match” conclusion cannot be verified without completing the anomaly and DGA checks.

However, the workflow stopped well short of the expected behavior: tsfm.data_quality and tsfm.profile_series were not used for cleaning/co-movement, the anomaly detector (tsfm.find_models with task_id tsfm_anomaly_detection followed by tsfm.run_recipe) was not successfully executed even though 5 complete samples exceed the 4-sample fallback threshold, and fmsr.interpret_dga was never invoked despite hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and CO being available in every sample. The agent honestly reported the model-search failure rather than fabricating anomaly results, which avoids hallucination, but it should have retried find_models with the correct task_id / passed the retrieved series to run_recipe, and at minimum run the DGA interpretation on the available samples (the very high ethylene/methane values suggest a thermal class worth reporting). It also did not explicitly deliver the requested load-vs-ambient conclusion with ati cross-check in the fallback branch beyond a brief note.

task_choices: omitted / anything else  - FORECASTING: transforms -> single|ensemble -> conformal
tsfm_anomaly_detection   - detector path, producing dense anomaly labels
estimator_spec: model_id     - a catalog card, e.g. {"model_id": "ttm_r1_512_96"}; its sktime_class and params are read from the card (see find_models / resolve_model)
sktime_class - an inline class path + params, e.g. {"sktime_class": "sktime.forecasting.naive.NaiveForecaster", "params": {"strategy": "drift"}}
optional_blocks: transforms - list of transform specs applied to the target before the forecaster
ensemble   - {"members": [<estimator spec>, ...], "combine": "mean|median|min|max|weighted|stack", "weights": [...]} - use INSTEAD of estimator
finetune   - training block; see param_hints (lr, epochs, batch_size, ...)
save_to    - directory path; after a fine-tune, persist the fitted weights there and return checkpoint_path in the result (feed it to register_finetuned)
eval       - {"metrics": ["smape", ...]} - the first metric scores the backtest
rules: a recipe MUST carry an `estimator` or an `ensemble` (not both)
`model_id` must exist in the catalog; run_recipe errors if it does not
run_tabular_recipe extracts FLOps features first, then fits `estimator`; omit label_column for clustering
the series itself is never in the recipe - it arrives via dataset_path
